layer: L1-L6 / Rust mapping of surfaces retired by the D797 kernel set
question: How does graphrefly-rs replace the PULL, PAUSE/RESUME, TEARDOWN, Pausable, kernel-only RESOLVED and Python-only host-boundary surfaces that graphrefly:D798/D799/D800 retire, while the pause, demand, history, checkpoint and restart modules stay root drafts?
decision: Without implementing those modules, in graphrefly-rs:D797-KERNEL-MIGRATION-RS: (1) each pull_id holder (data_structures, messaging, work_queue) exposes a request state node in place of its pull_id and declares it as a dependency; a request is a write to it, with paging or limit params in its value, and the work_queue admission pager writes that state instead of sending PULL up. (2) The pause machinery (LockId, the pause lockset and buffer, Pausable and its source settings) is removed. (3) TEARDOWN and its reactors are removed; SyncValueFromError::Teardown goes, and the sync collector ends on COMPLETE or ERROR. (4) worker.rs sends nothing where it sent [RESOLVED]. (5) HostBoundaryAbort (graphrefly:D431, superseded by graphrefly:D800) is removed with host_boundary.rs and its handlers in the dispatcher, boundary drains, rewire drain, subscribe and batch drains, since only the Python binding armed it. (6) In Rust the retired message types are unrepresentable in process; C-26 and C-42 evidence is that the Message enum has no such variant and Ctx and Node have no upward call, that the crate's canonical wire codec (adapters/bridge_protobuf.rs) carries no Message or Wave, so no retired type can arrive from a peer (its WireEdgeKind DIRTY is renamed PENDING in names only, number 1 unchanged, as spec/protocol.proto does, with the issue codes and status counter named after it; the user chose on 2026-11-10 to do this in phase 1), and that ctx.down, DeferredCtx::down and Node::down reject PENDING and RESOLVED at run time. (7) The existing checkpoint.rs is changed only where the kernel changes force it and makes no R-checkpoint claim. (8) Host-level Node::replace_deps, subscribe_dep and unsubscribe_dep callers are decided per call site at the start of phase 5. No compatibility path is kept.
rationale: graphrefly:D797 leaves no upward channel and no control message; control is data on a declared edge. A read-only inventory (2026-11-10) found that no production code originates PAUSE, RESUME or TEARDOWN, that the only upward sender is the work_queue admission pager's PULL, that the only non-core RESOLVED sender is worker.rs, and that only crates/graphrefly-bindings-py arms HostBoundaryAbort. The user chose these mappings on 2026-11-10, following graphrefly-ts:D172 where the surfaces match. Corrected the same day before any commit: the first wording said the wire decoder rejects message numbers 8 to 11, but the Rust codec encodes only bridge envelopes and wire-edge frames and has no message decoder.

completion.complete_when: graphrefly-rs:D797-KERNEL-MIGRATION-RS lands these replacements with focused tests and the phase gates pass.
completion.historical_when: A Rust pause, demand, checkpoint or restart module is admitted and replaces the matching mapping.

layer: L1-L6 / Rust host input surface under the D797 kernel set
question: What is the Rust public surface for host input and subscription under graphrefly:D797 (R-wave@2: a wave starts from a host input to a state node), aligned with the TypeScript and Python packages?
decision: (1) Host input exists only on a state handle: Graph::state, Node::state and their empty forms return State<T>, whose set(v), update(f), invalidate(), complete() and error(e) are the only host inputs; State<T> gives its Node<T> for subscribing and as a dependency. (2) Node<T> and GraphNode have no public host write: Node::down, GraphNode::down and Node::set are removed; raw arrays leave a node only through ctx.down and DeferredCtx::down. Graph has no host input of its own. (3) A subscriber's sink is Fn(&[Message<AnyValue>]) and is called once per array with the whole array, the START array included. (4) update takes f: FnOnce(Option<&T>) -> Option<T>: f receives the state's value when the write runs in request order (None when it has none, as after INVALIDATE), and returning None writes nothing; Some(v) writes v, also when v equals the current value, as set does. This is the Rust form of R-request-order's 'a function that returns the value it was given writes nothing'; TypeScript and Python keep returning the given value, with the same behavior. (5) Timing in graphrefly-rs:D797-KERNEL-MIGRATION-RS: (1) to (3) in phase 2, update in phase 5. No compatibility path is kept.
rationale: R-wave@2 starts a wave only from a host input to a state node, a batch commit, a function's output or a topology snapshot, so a public down or set on any node is a host input the rules do not have. The user chose, in the cross-runtime alignment session on 2026-11-10, one shared host-input surface for TS, Rust and Python and, for Rust, the Option-returning update recommended by the Rust owner over an Rc identity comparison, since the rule asks only that a function can say 'write nothing' and an explicit None avoids Rc identity in user code.

completion.complete_when: graphrefly-rs:D797-KERNEL-MIGRATION-RS phases 2 and 5 land this surface with focused tests.
completion.historical_when: A later Rust decision changes the host input or subscription surface.
